newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy government calls confidence vote.
newsitem.headline: Italy government calls confidence vote.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government on Wednesday called a confidence vote in the lower house of parliament on a civil service reform bill.

Regional Affairs Minister Franco Bassanini told parliament the measure had been taken to ensure passage of a bill already approved in the upper house, where the government has a majority, but hit by delaying tactics in the lower one.
The confidence vote is designed to sweep away amendments and approve with a simple vote those articles of the draft legislation that have yet to be passed.
No date was set for the confidence vote, which cannot take place until 24 hours after it was called.
Centre-left Prime Minister Romano Prodi does not have a majority in the lower house, where he relies on the support of hard-left Communist Refoundation allies.

Refoundation pushed the government to the brink of collapse last week when they voted against the deployment of an Italian-led security force for Albania. The force was approved with votes from the centre-right opposition.
